name: Relative Atomic Mass
expr: Ar = mass of atom / (1/12 mass of C-12)

name: Law of Conservation of Mass
expr: mass of reactants = mass of products

name: Law of Definite Proportions
expr: compound has fixed ratio of elements by mass

name: Limiting Reagent (concept)
expr: reagent that produces least product runs out first

name: Octet Rule
expr: atoms gain/lose/share e⁻ to have 8 valence e⁻

name: VSEPR (basic)
expr: electron pairs arrange to minimize repulsion

name: Le Chatelier's Principle
expr: system shifts to counter applied stress

name: Empirical Formula (organic)
expr: simplest whole-number mole ratio of elements

name: Buffer Capacity (concept)
expr: resists pH change on addition of acid/base

name: Law of Multiple Proportions
expr: masses of one element combine with fixed mass of other in small whole numbers

name: Law of Reciprocal Proportions
expr: ratio of masses combining with fixed mass of a third element

name: Common Ion Effect (concept)
expr: adding common ion shifts equilibrium, lowers solubility

name: Fugacity
expr: f = γP (effective pressure of real gas)

name: Retention Factor (Chromatography)
expr: Rf = distance by solute / distance by solvent

name: Aufbau Principle
expr: electrons fill lowest energy orbitals first

name: Pauli Exclusion Principle
expr: no two electrons share all 4 quantum numbers

name: Hund's Rule
expr: degenerate orbitals fill singly before pairing

name: Le Chatelier's Principle
expr: system shifts to counteract applied stress

name: Franck-Condon Principle
expr: electronic transitions occur with fixed nuclear positions

name: Coordination Number
expr: number of donor atoms bonded to central metal

name: Chelate Effect
expr: polydentate ligands form more stable complexes

name: Decay Series
expr: sequential α/β decays to a stable isotope

name: Markovnikov's Rule
expr: H adds to carbon with more H atoms

name: Overall Reaction Order
expr: order = sum of exponents (m + n) in rate law

name: Common Ion Effect on Ionization (concept)
expr: a common ion suppresses ionization of a weak acid or base

name: IUPAC Parent Chain Rule (concept)
expr: longest continuous carbon chain determines the parent name

name: Theoretical Yield (concept)
expr: maximum product calculated from the limiting reagent

name: Mass-to-Mass Stoichiometry
expr: mass B = (mass A/M_A) × mole ratio × M_B

name: Geometric Isomer Count (concept)
expr: cis/trans arrangements depend on ligand positions

name: Nuclear Stability (N/Z Ratio)
expr: N/Z ≈ 1 for light stable nuclei, increases for heavier ones

name: Gravimetric Factor
expr: GF = molar mass of analyte/molar mass of precipitate

name: Resonance Energy
expr: RE = actual bond energy − calculated bond energy

name: Carbon Footprint (concept)
expr: total CO₂-equivalent emissions from an activity

name: Equivalence Point (concept)
expr: moles of acid equal moles of base at stoichiometric ratio

name: Isotope Notation
expr: ᴬZX (A = mass number, Z = atomic number)

name: Electron Configuration Rule (concept)
expr: electrons fill orbitals from lowest to highest energy (Aufbau)

name: Ionization Energy Trend (concept)
expr: increases across a period, decreases down a group

name: Atomic Radius Trend (concept)
expr: decreases across a period, increases down a group

name: Electron Affinity (concept)
expr: energy released when an atom gains an electron

name: Molar Volume at STP
expr: 1 mole of gas = 22.4 L at STP

name: Total Dissolved Solids (concept)
expr: sum of all dissolved minerals and salts in water, in mg/L

name: pH Scale of Rainwater (concept)
expr: normal rainwater has pH about 5.6 due to dissolved CO2

name: COD (Chemical Oxygen Demand)
expr: amount of oxygen required to oxidize organic matter chemically

name: Ozone Depletion Reaction (concept)
expr: Cl radicals catalytically destroy ozone: Cl + O3 → ClO + O2

name: Conjugate Acid-Base Pair (concept)
expr: acid loses a proton to form its conjugate base

name: Amphoteric Species (concept)
expr: a substance that can act as both an acid and a base

name: Relationship Between Q and K (concept)
expr: Q<K forward shift, Q>K reverse shift, Q=K equilibrium

name: Cell Notation Convention (concept)
expr: anode | anode solution || cathode solution | cathode

name: Homologous Series (concept)
expr: members differ by a -CH2- unit and share similar properties

name: Markovnikov's Rule (simple statement)
expr: H adds to carbon with more H atoms already attached

name: Isomers Count (concept)
expr: compounds with same molecular formula, different structure

name: Peptide Bond Formation (concept)
expr: condensation of -COOH and -NH2 groups releasing H2O

name: Glycosidic Bond (concept)
expr: bond linking two monosaccharides formed by dehydration

name: ATP Hydrolysis Energy (concept)
expr: ATP + H2O → ADP + Pi, releases ~30.5 kJ/mol

name: Isoelectric Point (concept)
expr: pH at which a molecule carries no net electric charge

name: Haber Process (concept)
expr: N2 + 3H2 ⇌ 2NH3, high pressure with iron catalyst

name: Contact Process (concept)
expr: SO2 oxidized to SO3 using V2O5 catalyst, then converted to H2SO4

name: Atom Economy
expr: Atom Economy = (Mass of desired product/Mass of all reactants) × 100

name: Percent Atom Utilization
expr: (Molar mass of product/Sum molar mass of reactants) × 100

name: Oxidation Number Rule (Complex Ion)
expr: sum of oxidation states of ligands and metal = overall charge

name: Werner's Theory (concept)
expr: metal ions have primary and secondary valencies in complexes

name: Degree of Dissociation from Van't Hoff Factor
Crystal Lattice Energy Trend (concept)
expr: increases with higher ionic charge and smaller ionic radius

name: Chromatography Rf Value
expr: Rf = Distance moved by solute/Distance moved by solvent

name: Degree of Unsaturation
expr: DoU = (2C + 2 + N − H)/2, C = carbons, N = nitrogens, H = hydrogens

name: Isomers (concept)
expr: compounds with the same molecular formula but different structural arrangements

name: Functional Group (concept)
expr: a specific group of atoms within a molecule responsible for its characteristic chemical reactions

name: Nucleophilic Substitution (SN1/SN2) (concept)
expr: reactions where a nucleophile replaces a leaving group; SN1 is stepwise, SN2 is a single concerted step

name: Electrophilic Addition (concept)
expr: an electrophile adds across a double or triple bond, typical of alkene/alkyne reactions

name: Elimination Reaction (E1/E2) (concept)
expr: a reaction that removes atoms from a molecule to form a double bond, releasing a small byproduct

name: Markovnikov's Rule (concept)
expr: in addition to an unsymmetrical alkene, H adds to the carbon with more hydrogens already attached

name: Esterification Reaction (concept)
expr: Carboxylic Acid + Alcohol ⇌ Ester + Water (catalyzed by acid)

name: Saponification Reaction (concept)
expr: Ester + Strong Base → Soap (carboxylate salt) + Alcohol

name: Aromaticity (Hückel's Rule)
expr: a ring is aromatic if it is planar, cyclic, fully conjugated, and has (4n+2) π electrons

name: Chirality / Optical Isomerism (concept)
expr: a molecule with a carbon bonded to four different groups can exist as non-superimposable mirror images

name: Polymerization (concept)
expr: the process of joining many small monomer molecules together to form a large polymer chain

name: Limiting Reagent (concept)
expr: the reactant that is completely consumed first, limiting the amount of product formed

name: Theoretical Yield (concept)
expr: the maximum amount of product that could be formed from the limiting reagent, based on stoichiometry

name: Percent Composition
expr: Percent Composition = (Mass of Element in Compound/Molar Mass of Compound) × 100

name: Empirical Formula (concept)
expr: the simplest whole-number ratio of atoms of each element in a compound

name: Molecular Formula from Empirical Formula
expr: Molecular Formula = (Empirical Formula)ₙ, n = Molar Mass/Empirical Formula Mass

name: Molar Mass
expr: Molar Mass = Mass of Substance (g)/Number of Moles

name: Number of Particles from Moles
expr: N = n × Nₐ, Nₐ = Avogadro's Number (6.022 × 10²³)

name: Molar Volume of a Gas at STP
expr: 1 mole of any gas occupies 22.4 L at STP

name: Hess's Law
expr: the total enthalpy change for a reaction is the same regardless of the number of steps taken

name: Enthalpy of Formation (concept)
expr: the heat change when 1 mole of a compound forms from its elements in their standard states

name: Enthalpy of Combustion (concept)
expr: the heat released when 1 mole of a substance burns completely in oxygen

name: Bond Enthalpy Calculation
expr: ΔH = Σ(Bond Energies Broken) − Σ(Bond Energies Formed)

name: Calorimetry Heat Formula
expr: q = mcΔT, m = mass, c = specific heat capacity, ΔT = temperature change

name: Exothermic vs Endothermic (concept)
expr: exothermic reactions release heat (ΔH negative); endothermic reactions absorb heat (ΔH positive)

name: Specific Heat Capacity (concept)
expr: the amount of heat needed to raise the temperature of 1 g of a substance by 1°C

name: Elevation in Boiling Point
expr: ΔTb = Kb × m, Kb = molal boiling point constant, m = molality

name: Depression in Freezing Point
expr: ΔTf = Kf × m, Kf = molal freezing point constant

name: Osmotic Pressure (Van't Hoff Equation)
expr: π = MRT, M = molarity, R = gas constant, T = temperature (K)

name: Van't Hoff Factor
expr: i = Actual number of particles in solution/Number of formula units initially dissolved

name: Molality
expr: m = Moles of Solute/Mass of Solvent (kg)

name: Mole Fraction
expr: X_A = Moles of A/Total Moles of All Components

name: Isotonic Solutions (concept)
expr: two solutions with equal osmotic pressure, causing no net water movement between them

name: Faraday's First Law of Electrolysis
expr: Mass Deposited ∝ Quantity of Charge Passed (Q = It)

name: Faraday's Second Law of Electrolysis
expr: for the same charge, mass deposited is proportional to the equivalent weight of the substance

name: Gibbs Free Energy and Cell Potential
Molar Conductivity
expr: Λm = κ/C, κ = specific conductivity, C = molar concentration

name: Galvanic vs Electrolytic Cell (concept)
expr: a galvanic cell generates electricity from a spontaneous reaction; an electrolytic cell uses electricity to drive a non-spontaneous reaction

name: Photochemical Reaction (concept)
expr: a chemical reaction initiated by the absorption of light energy

name: Energy of a Photon
expr: E = hν = hc/λ, h = Planck's constant, ν = frequency, λ = wavelength

name: Quantum Yield (Photochemistry)
expr: Φ = Number of Molecules Reacted/Number of Photons Absorbed

name: Photosynthesis Light Reactions (concept)
expr: light energy is absorbed by chlorophyll and converted into chemical energy (ATP and NADPH)

name: Fluorescence vs Phosphorescence (concept)
expr: fluorescence emits light almost instantly after absorption; phosphorescence emits it over a longer delayed period

name: Green Chemistry (concept)
expr: the design of chemical products and processes that reduce or eliminate hazardous substances

name: Atom Economy
expr: Atom Economy = (Molar Mass of Desired Product/Total Molar Mass of Reactants) × 100

name: E-Factor (Environmental Factor)
expr: E-Factor = Mass of Waste/Mass of Desired Product

name: Renewable Feedstock (concept)
expr: raw materials derived from replenishable biological sources rather than fossil fuels

name: Biodegradability (concept)
expr: the ability of a substance to be broken down naturally by microorganisms without harming the environment

name: Catalysis in Green Chemistry (concept)
expr: catalysts speed up reactions and reduce energy requirements and waste production

name: Caloric Value of Macronutrients (concept)
expr: Carbohydrates and Proteins ≈ 4 kcal/g, Fats ≈ 9 kcal/g

name: Maillard Reaction (concept)
expr: a chemical reaction between amino acids and reducing sugars that browns food and creates flavor when heated

name: Rancidity (concept)
expr: the oxidative or hydrolytic decomposition of fats/oils, producing unpleasant odors and taste

name: pH of Common Foods (concept)
expr: most foods are mildly acidic; e.g. lemon juice ≈ pH 2, milk ≈ pH 6.5

name: Preservatives (concept)
expr: substances added to food to prevent microbial spoilage and extend shelf life

name: Emulsification (concept)
expr: the process of mixing two immiscible liquids (e.g. oil and water) into a stable dispersion

name: Forensic Chemistry (concept)
expr: the application of chemical analysis techniques to identify substances relevant to criminal investigations

name: Chromatography in Forensics (concept)
expr: separates mixtures (e.g. drugs, inks) into components based on differing movement through a stationary phase

name: Mass Spectrometry (concept)
expr: identifies compounds by measuring the mass-to-charge ratio of ionized fragments

name: Blood Alcohol Content (BAC) (concept)
expr: the percentage of alcohol present in a person's bloodstream, used in toxicology testing

name: Presumptive vs Confirmatory Tests (concept)
expr: presumptive tests give a quick, tentative result; confirmatory tests provide definitive identification

name: Luminol Test (concept)
expr: a chemical test that produces a blue glow when it reacts with the iron in hemoglobin, detecting trace blood

name: Adsorption (concept)
expr: the adhesion of molecules from a gas or liquid to a solid or liquid surface, forming a thin film

name: Absorption vs Adsorption (concept)
expr: absorption is uptake throughout the bulk of a material; adsorption occurs only at the surface

name: Freundlich Adsorption Isotherm
expr: x/m = kP^(1/n), x/m = mass adsorbed per unit mass of adsorbent, P = pressure

name: Langmuir Adsorption Isotherm
expr: θ = KP/(1 + KP), θ = fraction of surface covered

name: Colloid (concept)
expr: a mixture where microscopically dispersed particles (1–1000 nm) are suspended throughout another substance

name: Tyndall Effect (concept)
expr: the scattering of light by particles in a colloid, making the light beam visible

name: Brownian Motion (concept)
expr: the random, erratic movement of colloidal particles caused by collisions with solvent molecules

name: Emulsion (concept)
expr: a colloidal dispersion of one liquid within another immiscible liquid, stabilized by an emulsifier

name: Micelle Formation (concept)
expr: surfactant molecules aggregate above a critical concentration, orienting hydrophobic tails inward

name: Critical Micelle Concentration (CMC) (concept)
expr: the surfactant concentration above which micelles begin to form spontaneously

name: Unit Cell (concept)
expr: the smallest repeating structural unit of a crystal lattice

name: Bragg's Law
expr: nλ = 2d sinθ, used in X-ray diffraction to determine crystal spacing

name: Density of Unit Cell
expr: ρ = ZM/(Nₐ × a³), Z = number of atoms per cell, M = molar mass, a = edge length

name: Coordination Number (Crystal Lattice) (concept)
expr: the number of nearest neighboring atoms/ions surrounding a given atom or ion in a crystal

name: Crystal Defects (concept)
expr: irregularities in a crystal lattice, such as vacancies, interstitials, and substitutions

name: Fractional Distillation of Crude Oil (concept)
expr: separates crude oil into fractions based on differing boiling points of hydrocarbons

name: Octane Number (concept)
expr: a measure of a fuel's resistance to knocking during combustion in a gasoline engine

name: Calorific Value of Fuel (concept)
expr: the amount of heat released when a unit mass of fuel is completely combusted

name: Cracking (Petrochemistry) (concept)
expr: breaking down large hydrocarbon molecules into smaller, more useful ones using heat, pressure, or catalysts

name: Biofuel (concept)
expr: fuel derived from recently living biological material, such as ethanol from crops

name: Combustion Reaction (General)
expr: Fuel + O₂ → CO₂ + H₂O + Energy (complete combustion)

name: Drug Design (concept)
expr: the process of finding new medications based on the biological structure of a target molecule

name: Structure-Activity Relationship (SAR) (concept)
expr: the relationship between a molecule's chemical structure and its biological activity

name: Prodrug (concept)
expr: an inactive compound that is metabolized in the body into its active pharmaceutical form

name: Racemic Mixture (concept)
expr: an equal mixture of two enantiomers of a chiral molecule, often with differing biological activity

name: Solubility and Drug Absorption (concept)
expr: a drug's solubility strongly affects how well and how quickly it is absorbed into the bloodstream

name: pKa and Drug Ionization
expr: pH = pKa + log([A⁻]/[HA]), determines the ionized/unionized ratio of a drug at a given pH

name: Excipient (concept)
expr: an inactive substance formulated alongside the active drug to aid in its manufacture or delivery

name: Controlled Drug Release (concept)
expr: formulation technology designed to release a drug gradually over an extended period

name: Crystal Field Splitting Energy (Octahedral)
expr: Δo = 10 Dq, splitting of d-orbitals in an octahedral ligand field

name: Crystal Field Stabilization Energy (CFSE) (concept)
expr: the extra stability a transition metal complex gains from electrons occupying lower-energy d-orbitals

name: Lattice Energy (concept)
expr: the energy released when gaseous ions combine to form one mole of an ionic solid, proportional to (Q1×Q2)/r

name: Coordination Number (concept)
expr: the number of ligand donor atoms directly bonded to a central metal atom or ion

name: Hard and Soft Acids and Bases (HSAB) (concept)
expr: hard acids/bases prefer to bond with other hard species, and soft acids/bases prefer soft species

name: Jahn-Teller Effect (concept)
expr: a geometric distortion in certain electronic configurations that removes orbital degeneracy and lowers energy

name: Diagonal Relationship (concept)
expr: similarity in properties between an element and the element diagonally below-right of it in the periodic table

name: Effective Nuclear Charge (Slater's Rules)
expr: Z_eff = Z − S, Z = atomic number, S = screening constant

name: Ionic Radius Trend (concept)
expr: ionic radius decreases across a period and increases down a group, due to effective nuclear charge and added shells

name: 18-Electron Rule
expr: stable organometallic complexes tend to have a total of 18 valence electrons around the metal center

name: Oxidative Addition (concept)
expr: a reaction where a metal center increases its oxidation state and coordination number by inserting into a bond

name: Reductive Elimination (concept)
expr: a reaction where a metal center decreases its oxidation state and coordination number, releasing a new bond

name: Migratory Insertion (concept)
expr: a step where a ligand migrates to an adjacent coordinated group, forming a new bond without changing oxidation state

name: Hapticity (concept)
expr: ηⁿ notation describing the number of contiguous ligand atoms bonded to a metal center

name: Metal Carbonyl Bonding (concept)
expr: synergic bonding between CO and a metal involving σ-donation from CO and π-back donation from the metal

name: Catalytic Cycle (concept)
expr: a repeating sequence of elementary steps in which a catalyst is regenerated after converting reactants to products

name: Drug-Receptor Interaction (concept)
expr: the binding of a drug molecule to a specific biological receptor to produce a pharmacological effect

name: Lipinski's Rule of Five (concept)
expr: predicts oral drug-likeness based on molecular weight, lipophilicity, and hydrogen bond donors/acceptors

name: Bioavailability
expr: F = (AUC oral/AUC IV) × 100, the fraction of an administered drug that reaches systemic circulation

name: Pharmacophore (concept)
expr: the arrangement of molecular features necessary for a drug to interact with its biological target

name: IC50 (concept)
expr: the concentration of a drug required to inhibit a biological process by 50%

name: ED50 (concept)
expr: the dose of a drug that produces a therapeutic effect in 50% of a population

name: Drug Metabolism — ADME (concept)
expr: Absorption, Distribution, Metabolism, Excretion — the four stages describing a drug's journey through the body

name: Retention Factor (Rf)
expr: Rf = Distance traveled by solute/Distance traveled by solvent

name: Retention Time (concept)
expr: the time a compound takes to pass through a chromatography column and reach the detector

name: Column Chromatography (concept)
expr: a technique separating compounds based on differential adsorption as they pass through a packed column

name: Thin Layer Chromatography (TLC) (concept)
expr: a technique separating compounds on a thin adsorbent layer coated on a plate, based on polarity

name: Gas Chromatography (concept)
expr: a technique separating volatile compounds based on their interaction with a stationary phase in a gas-flow column

name: HPLC (High-Performance Liquid Chromatography) (concept)
expr: a technique using high pressure to force a liquid sample through a column for precise separation and analysis

name: Resolution (Chromatography)
expr: Rs = 2(tR2 − tR1)/(w1 + w2), measures separation between two adjacent peaks

name: Partition Coefficient
expr: K = Concentration in Stationary Phase/Concentration in Mobile Phase

name: Mass-to-Charge Ratio (m/z) (concept)
expr: the ratio of an ion's mass to its charge, plotted on the x-axis of a mass spectrum

name: Molecular Ion Peak (concept)
expr: the peak corresponding to the unfragmented molecule that has lost one electron

name: Base Peak (concept)
expr: the tallest peak in a mass spectrum, assigned a relative intensity of 100%

name: Fragmentation Pattern (concept)
expr: the characteristic set of ion peaks produced when a molecule breaks apart during ionization

name: Isotope Pattern (concept)
expr: the relative peak intensities in a mass spectrum arising from an element's naturally occurring isotopes

name: Resolving Power (Mass Spectrometry)
expr: RP = m/Δm, m = mass of the ion, Δm = smallest resolvable mass difference

name: Nitrogen Rule (concept)
expr: a molecule with an odd number of nitrogen atoms has an odd nominal molecular mass, and vice versa

name: Molecular Mechanics (concept)
expr: models molecular energy using classical physics with force fields, treating atoms as balls and bonds as springs

name: Ab Initio Methods (concept)
expr: quantum chemistry calculations based purely on fundamental physical constants, without empirical parameters

name: Density Functional Theory (DFT) (concept)
expr: a computational method that determines molecular properties using electron density rather than the full wavefunction

name: Basis Set (concept)
expr: a set of mathematical functions used to approximate molecular orbitals in computational calculations

name: Potential Energy Surface (concept)
expr: a multidimensional surface representing a molecule's energy as a function of its atomic coordinates

name: Molecular Dynamics Simulation (concept)
expr: simulates the physical movement of atoms and molecules over time by numerically solving Newton's equations of motion

name: Hartree-Fock Method (concept)
expr: an approximate method for determining the wavefunction and energy of a many-electron system

name: Corrosion (concept)
expr: the gradual destruction of a material, usually a metal, through chemical or electrochemical reaction with its environment

name: Rusting Reaction
expr: 4Fe + 3O₂ + 6H₂O → 4Fe(OH)₃, the electrochemical corrosion of iron in the presence of water and oxygen

name: Galvanic Corrosion (concept)
expr: accelerated corrosion of a less noble metal when it is in electrical contact with a more noble metal in an electrolyte

name: Corrosion Rate
expr: CR = (K × W)/(A × T × D), W = weight loss, A = area, T = time, D = density, K = constant

name: Cathodic Protection (concept)
expr: a technique preventing corrosion by making the metal surface the cathode of an electrochemical cell

name: Passivation (concept)
expr: the formation of a thin protective oxide layer on a metal surface that slows further corrosion

name: Pitting Corrosion (concept)
expr: localized corrosion that produces small holes or pits in a metal surface

name: Catalyst (concept)
expr: a substance that increases the rate of a chemical reaction without being consumed in the process

name: Homogeneous vs Heterogeneous Catalysis (concept)
expr: homogeneous catalysts are in the same phase as reactants; heterogeneous catalysts are in a different phase

name: Turnover Number (Catalysis)
expr: TON = Moles of Product/Moles of Catalyst

name: Enzyme as Biological Catalyst (concept)
expr: a protein catalyst that accelerates biochemical reactions by lowering activation energy

name: Autocatalysis (concept)
expr: a reaction in which one of the products acts as a catalyst for the reaction itself

name: Catalytic Poisoning (concept)
expr: the loss of catalytic activity caused by a substance binding to and blocking active sites

name: Activation Energy Lowering by Catalyst (concept)
expr: a catalyst provides an alternative reaction pathway with lower activation energy, increasing reaction rate

name: Hardness of Water (concept)
expr: water hardness results from dissolved calcium and magnesium ions, causing scale formation and reduced soap lathering

name: Total Dissolved Solids (TDS) (concept)
expr: the total concentration of dissolved organic and inorganic substances in water

name: Chlorination (concept)
expr: the addition of chlorine to water to disinfect it by killing bacteria and other pathogens

name: Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD) (concept)
expr: the amount of dissolved oxygen consumed by microorganisms decomposing organic matter in water

name: Chemical Oxygen Demand (COD) (concept)
expr: the amount of oxygen required to chemically oxidize both organic and inorganic matter in water

name: Reverse Osmosis (concept)
expr: a purification process that forces water through a semi-permeable membrane to remove ions, molecules, and larger particles

name: pH of Water and Water Quality (concept)
expr: safe drinking water typically has a pH between 6.5 and 8.5; values outside this range indicate contamination or imbalance

name: Unit Cell (concept)
expr: the smallest repeating structural unit of a crystal lattice that shows the full symmetry of the crystal

name: Bragg's Law
expr: nλ = 2d sinθ, relates X-ray wavelength, interplanar spacing, and diffraction angle

name: Miller Indices (concept)
expr: a notation system (hkl) used to describe the orientation of crystal planes

name: Packing Efficiency (concept)
expr: the percentage of a unit cell's volume actually occupied by its constituent atoms

name: Coordination Number in Crystal Lattices (concept)
expr: the number of nearest neighboring atoms or ions surrounding a given atom in a crystal structure

name: Avogadro's Number from Unit Cell
expr: N_A = (Z × M)/(ρ × a³), Z = atoms per cell, M = molar mass, ρ = density, a = edge length

name: Types of Unit Cells (concept)
expr: simple cubic, body-centered cubic (BCC), and face-centered cubic (FCC) are common cubic unit cell types

name: X-ray Diffraction (concept)
expr: a technique using the scattering of X-rays by a crystal lattice to determine its atomic structure

name: NPK Fertilizer Ratio (concept)
expr: the percentage by weight of Nitrogen (N), Phosphorus (P), and Potassium (K) in a fertilizer

name: Soil pH and Nutrient Availability (concept)
expr: soil pH strongly affects the solubility and availability of nutrients for plant uptake

name: Cation Exchange Capacity (CEC) (concept)
expr: a measure of a soil's ability to hold and exchange positively charged nutrient ions

name: Nitrogen Fixation in Soil (concept)
expr: the conversion of atmospheric nitrogen into ammonia by soil bacteria, making it usable by plants

name: Pesticide Residue (concept)
expr: the trace amount of pesticide that remains on or in food, soil, or water after application

name: Soil Organic Matter (concept)
expr: the decomposed plant and animal material in soil that improves fertility, structure, and water retention

name: Eutrophication (concept)
expr: excessive nutrient enrichment of water bodies, often from fertilizer runoff, causing algal blooms and oxygen depletion

name: Biofertilizer (concept)
expr: a substance containing living microorganisms that enhance nutrient availability when applied to soil or plants
